name: Stephen Miller
current_role: White House Chief of Staff (named November 6, 2026, starting November 9, 2026); Deputy Chief of Staff for Policy and Homeland Security Advisor since January 2025
summary: Stephen Miller is a Republican political aide and longtime adviser to Donald Trump, best known for shaping immigration policy. After working as a congressional press aide and for Sen. Jeff Sessions from 2009 to 2016, he was a senior White House policy adviser in Trump's first term, founded the conservative legal group America First Legal in 2021, and returned in 2025 as deputy chief of staff for policy. On November 6, 2026, Trump named him White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles.

connections.name: Jeff Sessions
connections.description: Miller joined Sen. Sessions's office as press secretary in June 2009 and became his communications director, writing speeches and working on immigration messaging, including the campaign against the 2013 bipartisan immigration bill. He left for the Trump campaign in January 2016, when Sessions was the first senator to endorse Trump.

connections.name: David Horowitz
connections.description: Horowitz is widely described as Miller's mentor. They met when Miller, as a Santa Monica High student, campaigned to bring Horowitz to speak at the school; at Duke, Miller led a chapter of Horowitz's Students for Academic Freedom. Horowitz says he recommended Miller for jobs with Rep. Michele Bachmann, Rep. John Shadegg and then Sen. Jeff Sessions. Miller praised Horowitz's legacy when he died in April 2025.

connections.name: Steve Bannon
connections.description: While working for Sessions, Miller cultivated close ties with Breitbart News under Bannon; leaked emails from 2015–2016 show Miller pitching and shaping Breitbart stories, with Bannon among the editors copied. They worked together in the early Trump White House, and Miller distanced himself from Bannon after Bannon's 2017 exit.

connections.name: Larry Elder
connections.description: As a Santa Monica High student Miller called in to Elder's Los Angeles talk-radio show and became a frequent guest; Elder has said he hosted Miller 69 times, and Miller cites Elder as an influence. Some accounts call Elder a mentor; NPR and Wikipedia describe him as an early influence and radio host rather than a formal mentor.

connections.name: Richard Spencer
connections.description: Disputed. Both were active in the Duke Conservative Union; Spencer says Miller helped with fundraising and promotion for a 2007 campus immigration debate Spencer organized, which another former member confirmed. Spencer has claimed he mentored Miller; Miller says he has 'absolutely no relationship' with Spencer and calls the claims '100 percent false.'
